messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] for-loop in R
messages.body_plain:
Hi Angelo,

Hmm, I'm not quite sure --- you seem to generally be on the right track.  The below worked for me.  If you're still having trouble, perhaps you could forward your code to me (either on list or privately)?

Cheers,

Josh

#######################################################
library(MplusAutomation)

# simulation stuff start
library(MASS)
set.seed(1234)
rmat.w <- matrix(.7, ncol = 3, nrow = 3)
diag(rmat.w) <- 1

rmat.b <- matrix(.4, ncol = 3, nrow = 3)
diag(rmat.b) <- 1

# 500 subjects
pop.b <- mvrnorm(n = 500, mu = c(0, 0, 0), Sigma = rmat.b)
# 20 observations each
pop.all <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:nrow(pop.b), function(i) {
                                       cbind(i, mvrnorm(n = 20, mu = c(0, 0, 0), Sigma = rmat.w) +
                                         do.call(rbind, rep(list(pop.b[i, ]), 20)))
                                     }))
colnames(pop.all) <- c("areas", "y1_a", "y2_a", "y3_a")

population <- as.data.frame(pop.all)
# simulation stuff end

model_a_s <- mplusObject(
  TITLE = "model_a",
  VARIABLE="CLUSTER=areas;
            ",
  ANALYSIS = "
      TYPE=twolevel;",
  MODEL = "
    %WITHIN%
       fw BY y1_a y2_a y3_a;

       %BETWEEN%
       fb BY y1_a y2_a y3_a;
    ",

  usevariables= c("areas","y1_a", "y2_a", "y3_a"),
  rdata = population,

  SAVEDATA = "
      file is scores_a_e.dat;
      save = fscores;
    ")

conditions <- expand.grid(Nsize=c(rep(1000,500)))

results_ex <- lapply(1:2, function(i) {

  sampdata_ex <- population[sample(1:nrow(population), size = conditions$Nsize[i]), ]
  mplusModeler(update(model_a_s, rdata = sampdata_ex),
             dataout = paste0("run_sample_", i, ".dat"),
             run = 1)
})

SummaryTable(results_ex,
             keepCols = c("Title", "LL", "Parameters", "AIC", "BIC", "SRMR.Within", "SRMR.Between"))

##      Title        LL Parameters      AIC      BIC SRMR.Within SRMR.Between
## 1  model_a -4322.903         15 8675.807 8749.423           0            0
## 2  model_a -4371.830         15 8773.660 8847.276           0            0
#######################################################

messages.subject: Re: MplusAutomation (extractTech10 function)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mariusz,

You are generally better off emailing the MplusAutomation group (cced here) for discussion, as other users see your question (and answer), plus both Michael and I monitor that list so you have a higher chance of a response.

The error you get is a red herring because you are calling a function that is not exported from the MplusAutomation package.  Generally, you readModels() to read in output files, which parses every portion of the file that we have functions to parse, rather than using functions to extract specific sections.

But the real issue is that as far as I know, although there is a skeleton function for extracting Tech10, that feature is not yet implemented in MplusAutomation.

If you or others were interested in working on implementing it, I'd be happy to mentor, but as none my "official" work generally uses mixture models, at the moment I do not have time to work on writing a parser for Tech10.  Michael may know more or have some idea if it is on his to-do list.

If you don't need all the information, it may be fairly simple to write something that reads in just one piece (e.g., total pearson chi-square from empty cells, or something like that).

Sorry its not better news!

Josh

--
Joshua Wiley, Ph.D.
Senior Analyst - Elkhart Group Ltd.
260.673.5518
jo...@elkhartgroup.com

messages.subject: problem with command DATA IMPUTATION
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a model, which runs without problem in MPlus and MplusAutomation. Now, if I add the command DATA IMPUTATION, it still runs in MPlus but not anymore in MplusAutomation:

In MPlus, the following syntax works:
DATA IMPUTATION:
impute f0f f0fl1 f0fl2 f0fl3 f0fl4 f0m f0ml1 f0ml2 f0ml3 f0ml4;
ndatasets=10;

But this syntax does not wirk for MplusAutomation:
DATA IMPUTATION = "
impute f0f f0fl1 f0fl2 f0fl3 f0fl4 f0m f0ml1 f0ml2 f0ml3 f0ml4;
ndatasets=10; ",

Any idea, why it does not work? Would be great to figure this out in order to be able to finalize the data analysis.

Thanks a lot!!!

Best,
Peter

messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] problem with command DATA IMPUTATION
messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter,

Sorry for the slow reply --- I don't do imputation in Mplus much so I had to look up a bit more about it.

I think that the issue is that there is not a DATA IMPUTATION "section" in mplusObject() function for now (I have added it to my to do list and will work on it when I get a chance).

In the mean time, one way around it is to just tack it on the end of the VARIABLE section, so for example:

m <- mplusObject(
  TITLE = "your title",
  VARIABLE = "
    USEVARIABLES = f0f f0fl1 f0fl2 f0fl3 f0fl4 f0m
      f0ml1 f0ml2 f0ml3 f0ml4;

  DATA IMPUTATION: ! need to add this heading for now until I update the package

  impute f0f f0fl1 f0fl2 f0fl3 f0fl4 f0m f0ml1 f0ml2 f0ml3 f0ml4;
  ndatasets=10;",

... <- analysis, model, etc.
)

and then carry on as usual.  Note that because mplusObject() does not have a section for it, you need to explicitly add the heading, whereas it normally does that for you.

Thanks for the catch!

Josh
